name: Legitimists
summary: Legitimists hold that the French crown belongs by hereditary right to the senior Bourbon line, overthrown in 1830, and reject both the Orleanist monarchy and the Republic. They are counter-revolutionary Catholic monarchists who favour hereditary kingship, Church influence, local liberties through administrative decentralisation, and, in the social Catholic strand, corporate bodies and class cooperation rather than liberal individualism or socialism.
scope: French Legitimism from 1830 to the death of the Count of Chambord in 1883, based on his 1871 manifesto and on the Legitimist-born social Catholicism of Albert de Mun and La Tour du Pin. It excludes the Orleanist and Bonapartist right and Action francaise nationalism, and treats the later Spanish-line (Blancs d'Espagne) claim as a dynastic variant. Answers on modern issues are mostly low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: Legitimist social Catholicism: workers' circles, labour reforms, rejection of socialism, class cooperation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: No Legitimist doctrine on health systems; paternalist Catholic charity and social Catholic reforms pull one way, aversion to state expansion the other.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: De Mun's social Catholics backed minimum wages and shorter hours, but this is a later strand, so only an inference for the wider camp.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Counter-revolutionary social Catholics rejected liberal laissez-faire as a revolutionary heritage, though they did not favour state economic control either.

public-ownership.rationale: Hostile to socialism as "logical Revolution"; they preferred corporate bodies and landed property to state ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Legitimism was the party of the landed aristocracy and notables, who would resist heavy taxes on wealth; not a documented programme.

unions-good.rationale: De Mun's circles favoured mixed bodies of employers and workers, and he backed legal unions in 1883, but class-based unions were not Legitimist doctrine.

property-fundamental.rationale: Landed property and hereditary inheritance underpinned the Ancien Regime order Legitimists wished to restore, which gives property strong protection.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Social Catholics wanted protective labour law, yet the camp never developed a position on modern corporations.

cut-welfare.rationale: Paternalist Catholic charity and social Catholic reform sit uneasily with welfare cuts; no stated Legitimist position either way.

worker-ownership.rationale: Social Catholics sought harmony of owners and workers through guilds and circles, not collective worker ownership, which they linked to socialism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Order-oriented and authoritarian-leaning monarchists would accept security measures; inferred only.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Catholic traditionalist moral order disfavours drug legalisation; anachronistic issue, inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Legitimists rejected liberal free-speech absolutism but the modern hate-speech question is anachronistic and adherents would split.

strong-leader.rationale: They favoured a hereditary king bound by tradition and local liberties, not a leader who bypasses institutions by force.

state-harmful.rationale: Monarchy is for them the basic form of government, with the king as indispensable executive, so rejecting the state itself is opposed.

limit-guns.rationale: Not an issue the doctrine addressed; no clear inference.

empower-police-military.rationale: Order-focused counter-revolutionaries would favour authority, though the army was traditionally the king's; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Catholic moral conservatism implies opposition; anachronistic, inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Chambord's 1871 manifesto promises a government founded on administrative decentralisation and local franchises under a strong king.

rehabilitation.rationale: No doctrine on penal philosophy; Catholic ideas of both penance and punishment apply.

traditional-family.rationale: Catholic traditionalism and dynastic hereditary principle make the family the base of society; consistent with Legitimist social conservatism.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Catholic traditionalist adherents, including modern ones, oppose it as contrary to Church teaching and traditional family order.

abortion-legal.rationale: Catholic traditionalism opposes abortion; modern Legitimists are Catholic traditionalists.

more-religion-public.rationale: Under the Restoration Legitimists passed the Anti-Sacrilege Act and the Falloux Law to expand Church influence.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a Legitimist issue; the anti-egalitarian, traditionalist outlook makes active redress unlikely.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Traditionalist Catholic view of natural sex roles opposes this; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Chambord's manifesto ties the white flag to national unity, Joan of Arc and the monarchy's historic heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: Legitimists sought restoration of the old order, which is not gradualism but is respect for established institutions; ambiguous.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Traditionalist and nationalist-leaning right; anachronistic issue, inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Dynastic and Catholic monarchists distrust modern supranational bodies; anachronistic.

free-trade.rationale: Landed aristocrats were often protectionist but there is no Legitimist trade doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: Chambord stresses French unity and honour, but no Legitimist programme on global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anachronistic; Catholic crusading sentiment against indifference to conservative sovereignty.

open-borders.rationale: Opposes dissolving national and dynastic identity; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: No Legitimist text addresses economic growth; neutral is the only honest answer from landed, Catholic principles that neither celebrate nor restrict it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy post-dates the movement; nothing in its principles favours or opposes large state programmes here, so neutral.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Counter-revolutionary scepticism of progress narratives; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic with no principle to infer from.

revolution-justified.rationale: Legitimism is defined by counter-revolution and rejection of the 1830 and 1789 revolutions; Chambord refused to be "king of the Revolution".

experts-over-public.rationale: They preferred hereditary and notable rule to mass democracy, but not technocracy.

central-planning.rationale: De Mun called socialism logical revolution; decentralist monarchists reject central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Opposed socialism and worker collectivisation, though little said on markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Landed notables would oppose a tax threatening landowners; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Hereditary transmission of property and crown is core; heavy inheritance taxes cut against it.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; unconditional state transfers conflict with paternalist, duty-based social Catholic thought.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Landed Legitimists had agrarian interests but no documented trade or industrial protection doctrine, so adherents are split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Decentralist; no support for central state economic direction.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Social Catholic and Le Play-school thinking favoured family property and rooted ownership; modest inference.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Such a position is socialist; Legitimists called socialism the Revolution.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Central banking was not a Legitimist concern, and neither monarchist nor social Catholic sources take a stance on money supply.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: La Tour du Pin, Legitimist at heart, was the leading French corporatist; de Mun's circles joined employers and workers.

one-party-rule.rationale: Legitimists defended the monarchical principle, not party rule, and worked within parliament via the Party of Order.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary monarchy is the basic form of government in Legitimist doctrine.

democracy-best.rationale: They rejected liberalism and republican and democratic ideas in principle.

direct-votes.rationale: Rejected democratic ideas; direct voting on laws is more so.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power is socialist and anti-hierarchical; opposed as revolution.

right-to-secede.rationale: Chambord stresses national unity, though decentralist; no statement on secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Hereditary succession by the senior line presumes that blood and lineage confer the right to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: They fought for restoration in the 1832 Vendee tradition and view counter-revolutionary force as justified; Chambord himself relied on constitutional means.

war-builds-character.rationale: Chambord invokes past glory but the sources show no doctrine that war ennobles a nation, leaving this neutral.

separate-church-state.rationale: Legitimists backed the Church's influence and the Catholic king; separation is the revolutionary-republican position.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Catholic natural law and Church teaching shape law but not literal scripture-based law; adherents lean positive yet split.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The king's justice and sovereign state are central; privatising them contradicts monarchy.

military-superiority.rationale: Chambord appeals to national honour and past conquests; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The French monarchy was dynastic and Catholic, not ethnic; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Counter-revolutionaries denied class struggle, embracing harmony of orders; de Mun explicitly opposed socialism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchical Ancien Regime society rejects enforced equality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land claims were never discussed by the camp; no principle points clearly either way.

civilizational-union.rationale: Catholic Christendom ideals exist but not as programme.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Catholic social ethics stress duty and charity over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Social Catholic and counter-revolutionary thought rejects the Revolution's individual rights in favour of duties within the social order.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is outside the Legitimist sources; Catholic creation theology could support or merely stay silent on it.

limit-population.rationale: Catholic opposition to contraception and coercive population control.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Some agrarian nostalgia but no documented Legitimist position.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Hostile to disruption of existing institutions; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Catholic moral traditionalism opposes it; anachronistic.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; conflicts with personal royal rule.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A digital-age question with nothing in dynastic Catholic monarchism to settle it; left neutral.

restore-past-order.rationale: Ultra-royalists sought to restore the Ancien Regime and reverse the Revolution; this defines the camp.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Principled doctrine of legitimacy over pragmatism: Chambord refused compromise on the flag despite the throne offered.

direct-action.rationale: Legitimists worked through parliament and royal restoration, not direct action, as in the Party of Order.

means-match-ends.rationale: Legitimists defended royal restoration and counter-revolution without a doctrine that methods must mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Obviously foreign to a landed Catholic monarchism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Catholic charity yes, but as a right of need under socialism no.

production-for-use.rationale: This is a socialist slogan; Legitimist social Catholics wanted ordered property and employers kept in place, so mild disagreement is inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: De Mun rejected socialism's analysis though he criticised industrial abuses.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Counter-revolution is the opposite of this.

collective-farming.rationale: Landed property and rooted peasantry rather than collectivism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Monarchy is a sovereign state authority that taxes; rejection is anarcho-capitalist.

harm-principle.rationale: Moral-order traditionalism holds the state may enforce virtue.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Counter-revolution rejected Revolutionary individualism for corporate bodies and communities.

conscription.rationale: The sources document no Legitimist view on military service; royalists favoured a royal army but split on universal service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The ideology rejects both democratic voting and a market of states, and no source ranks exit against voice, so neutral.

state-as-business.rationale: Monarchy rests on sovereignty and dynastic duty, not customer relations.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social Catholics supported protective labour reforms but never framed freedom this way.

media-academia-power.rationale: Counter-revolutionary suspicion of intellectual elites; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial genetics is not part of the doctrine, which grounds rule in dynastic lineage and Catholic universalism, so neutral on the empirical claim.

organic-representation.rationale: Albert de Mun's corporatist social Catholicism and Chambord's local franchises point to representation by communities and trade bodies rather than parties.

total-state.rationale: Decentralisation and local franchises are a Chambord programme, the opposite of a total state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Chambord promised to bring order and freedom after defeat; restoration, not radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Chambord stresses fidelity of Alsace and Lorraine but there is no expansionist doctrine.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Dynastic loyalty central, feudal oaths not stated; Chambord denied wishing to revive feudal rights.

bound-labor.rationale: Chambord explicitly denied intention to revive tithes and feudal rights as slander.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Catholic natural law implies universal truth.

universal-morality.rationale: Catholic natural-law tradition of Legitimist thinkers affirms universal truths.

single-common-good.rationale: Corporatist and social Catholic thought aims at a common good and harmony of orders over interest-group balance.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism sits outside Legitimist sources entirely; adherents would not agree on it, so neutral.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The question of diaspora return is not addressed in Legitimist sources; it is a candidate statement with no inferable position.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a Legitimist theme; the French monarchy's own languages policy offers no clear line.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Social Catholic circles favoured cooperation under owners, not democratic firm control.

school-vouchers.rationale: The Falloux Law expanded Church schooling; support for choice in education follows.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy was not doctrinal for Legitimists, and aristocratic debt-averseness is only a loose inference, so neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: The camp opposed liberal individualism but defended property; no source ties political freedom to economic freedom, so neutral.

rule-by-example.rationale: Chambord speaks of devotion and personal honour in the monarch; monarchist moral leadership inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Dynastic legitimacy, not popular nationhood, is the source of right.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN post-dates the doctrine and there is no principle about legal approval for force abroad that could settle it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Catholic traditionalism puts faith and tradition above Enlightenment rationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Immigrant welfare entitlement is a modern debate with no Legitimist source; social Catholic charity could cut either way.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is not discussed; paternalist charity and work ethic both appear in social Catholicism, so adherents split.

class-collaboration.rationale: De Mun's workers' circles united owners and workers; Legitimist social Catholicism rejected class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Defence of inherited institutions is central to counter-revolution.

dominated-front.rationale: A common front of states dominated by the West is a post-colonial idea with no Legitimist counterpart.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; rejects class politics in general.

ban-interest.rationale: Old Catholic usury doctrine exists, but 19th-century social Catholics did not press it uniformly.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not part of French Catholic monarchism; universalist Catholicism disagrees.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist thesis rejected by counter-revolutionary social Catholics.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for this movement and no principle favours one source over another.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement theory is not part of Legitimist sources; it is neither endorsed nor addressed there.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems were secondary to a movement that preferred hereditary monarchy and corporate representation, so neutral.

national-mission.rationale: France's historic Catholic mission exists in rhetoric but unstated here.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Traditionalist Catholic Legitimists take sex roles as natural and ordered, so they would deny that society structurally disadvantages women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Legitimists criticised the republican and Orleanist regimes yet are themselves notables.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Legal accountability for past state killings is not addressed in the sources; a royalist might point to royal justice but views vary.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Catholic monarchists favour state involvement in morals, religion and social order.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Catholic universalism and the dynastic monarchy's history give no basis for this, so mild disagreement is inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Catholic doctrine affirms equal worth before God, though against equal rights before the law in an estates order; split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The theory of settler colonialism is outside Legitimist thought and no principle settles it.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Corporate and religious bodies keep standing in a traditional order.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Catholic confessional monarchy favoured religious establishment, yet no source says conversion should be legally restricted, so split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A concern of Hindu politics with no link to French Catholic royalism; mild disagreement inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Falloux Law expanded Church role in schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist thesis about the socialist state; Legitimists opposed socialism, so they would reject it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Chambord grounded authority in the national principle of monarchical heredity, refusing to be king of the Revolution.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export surpluses are not a Legitimist theme; the sources carry no trade doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: Forcing a minority out contradicts Catholic universalist ethics and the dynasty's traditional framework, so mild disagreement is inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Legitimists accept force by lawful authority and counter-revolution, so they would not hold this absolute libertarian principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Catholic harmony ethos against struggle.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Monarchists favoured defensive order measures; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: No position; they sought local franchises.

separated-powers.rationale: Rejected constitutional limits on royal power, yet favoured local liberties.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social Catholics prioritised workers' welfare as Christian duty.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are a modern British policy, outside the sources; no principle decides it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Class-collaboration favours restricting strikes, but De Mun backed unions; mild.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Social Catholics blamed institutions and moral failings.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The sources say nothing on ethnic diversity; Catholic universalism and national unity concerns pull in different directions.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Hereditary and appointed offices, not chance.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Split between order and anti-arbitrary traditions.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Old-regime paternalism implies sympathy, not documented.

party-controls-media.rationale: They defended Church media, not party control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Legitimists place the army under the king, not a party; party command of forces is a communist arrangement they would reject.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship timelines are not addressed; a conservative, nation-minded outlook suggests mild agreement.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Notables were unpaid but not egalitarian.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding party discipline is a Leninist norm; Legitimists were notables in loose royalist blocs, so mild disagreement.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The hereditary monarch is the indispensable executive in Legitimist doctrine and opposed limits on royal power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Catholic doctrine governs the Church through bishops, and Legitimists were committed Catholic traditionalists backing Church authority.

clerical-rule.rationale: Catholic monarchism puts a king with Church influence, not clerics ruling.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The question concerns presidents, whom Legitimists reject.

recall-officials.rationale: Democratic device alien to the doctrine.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliances are not discussed in the sources, so adherents have no settled view on withdrawal.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Compulsory home ownership for all is a radical scheme alien to the landed order Legitimists defended, which relied on tenancy.

people-in-arms.rationale: An armed citizenry replacing the army is a republican idea; the Legitimist sources do not discuss it, so a mild no is inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Legitimism's base lay in provincial landed France, so a positive view of rural life is a plausible but unstated inference.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectual populism is not documented for the Legitimists, who were often educated notables themselves.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Traditionalist Catholics would oppose state sex education and gender-equality curricula, inferred from their view of Church control of schooling.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Evolution teaching is a later controversy; Catholic Legitimists have no documented line and adherents differ.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The Catholic moral order supported legal limits on obscenity, so agreement is inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: A dynastic movement grounded in lineage would favour descent over birthplace, but this is inferred rather than documented.

minority-language-support.rationale: The 1871 manifesto's call for local franchises and decentralisation implies tolerance of local languages, but not explicitly.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions for minorities are a liberal concept not discussed by Legitimists, who backed a Catholic establishment.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's call for eccentricity runs against the Legitimist reverence for custom and tradition, so mild disagreement.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt is anachronistic, and nothing in the principles points either way.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A post-colonial argument about economic transformation, with no Legitimist counterpart.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Chambord refused to be king of the Revolution, rejecting a regime founded on assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Developmental authoritarianism is not addressed in sources and Legitimists never framed policy this way.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Catholic charity exists but not specified.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons post-date the movement and no source gives guidance.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state in Legitimist doctrine is the hereditary king, so popular election of the head of state is flatly opposed.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed by the Legitimist sources, so neutral.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Chambord lauds Alsace-Lorraine but no doctrine.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Social Catholic doctrine ties property to social duty.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet debate between Marxists is outside Legitimist concerns, and no source offers a view.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation principle is modern; no Legitimist position or clear inference.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance guarantees such as NATO's post-date Legitimism and no principle decides the matter.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Chambord laments loss of Alsace-Lorraine, but no doctrine.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Legitimists backed the Church's power and wealth, as under the Restoration.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: King above parties by dynastic right, though they opposed purely ceremonial monarchy.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Chambord's decentralism favours local liberties, but he also prizes national unity forged under the monarchy, leaving adherents split.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine right monarchy is in the tradition, but Chambord denied absolutism; divine descent not claimed.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not a documented Legitimist concern, so neutral.

character-from-environment.rationale: No doctrine on this; inferred from a counter-revolutionary Catholic outlook that grounds right in lineage and inherited station rather than circumstance.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Legitimists defended a monarchy bound by the old fundamental laws and local franchises, as in Chambord's manifesto, though they rejected constitutional limits imposed by parliaments; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Legitimism predates and never addressed space; no basis in its principles to favour or oppose it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Legitimists rejected constitutional and parliamentary government in favour of hereditary kingship with decentralised local liberties; inferred, since a mixed regime with a strong assembly was the Orleanist model.

leader-cult.rationale: Legitimists venerated the person and symbols of the king, such as the white flag, as embodying the nation, but mass praise of a leader is a modern form they never practised; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the paternalist Catholic family order of the social Catholic strand.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The social Catholic strand of Albert de Mun sought class cooperation, rejecting class struggle.

land-redistribution.rationale: Legitimists were landed notables defending property, hierarchy and the traditional order against revolution.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Legitimists were dynastic, not ethnic nationalists; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: counter-revolutionary Catholics wanted Church influence but 19th-century law no longer punished apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from their social conservatism, but a legal mandate is outside what is documented.

common-currency.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from attachment to a French crown and national sovereignty.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Legitimism was tied to the French dynasty and nation; inferred opposition to merging peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Chambord favored administrative decentralisation and local liberties but the statement concerns national minorities; inferred neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: As counter-revolutionary Catholics they saw history as shaped by Providence, order and ideas, not production; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporate bodies and guild-like orders were favored but competition law is unaddressed; inferred neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They rejected popular sovereignty and majority rule, but did not defend independent courts; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from their hierarchical, family-centered social order.

moral-incentives.rationale: Social Catholics like de Mun stressed duty and Christian charity between classes over pure self-interest; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Legitimists took up arms in 1832 for the senior line but were chiefly counter-revolutionary; the claim is not addressed directly.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary kingship and privilege are the core of Legitimism, defended against the 1830 revolution.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the counter-revolutionary attachment to France's historic monarchy and Catholic heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from Catholic monarchist paternalism and the 1830 Algiers expedition under Charles X; Legitimists had no explicit doctrine on this.

patriotic-education.rationale: Chambord's manifesto stresses loyalty to the nation's historic flag and tradition, and Legitimists wanted Church-guided schooling.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The 19th-century Legitimists never addressed the issue, and a hierarchical outlook gives no clear lean either way.

public-money-creation.rationale: Social Catholics like La Tour du Pin distrusted finance, but nothing commits Legitimists to a public monopoly on money.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred from La Tour du Pin and de Mun, who thought liberal capitalism needed corporate reform and was socially destructive.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from Legitimist nostalgia for royal France, though the Restoration states had no such program.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from social Catholic corporatism, which favored national economic organization over free integration.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred from social Catholicism, which stressed class cooperation and shared interests of workers and employers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from paternalist Catholic social order, which put social duties above unrestricted private choice, though they also opposed state expansion.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Chambord's manifesto rejects the revolutionary principles of 1789 and rests rights on tradition and the crown, not a written entrenched charter.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Legitimists defend inherited rights and historical continuity, including treaties; but Chambord's decentralisation stance gives some sympathy to peoples; inferred, no direct stance.

elective-rulers.rationale: Legitimism rests on hereditary succession to the senior Bourbon line and rejects elected rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: Legitimists favour a corporate, hierarchical order and the unity of the crown; inferred that individual vetoes are rejected, with local franchises as the counterweight.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Legitimists backed traditional, limited monarchy under natural law, but rejected popular sovereignty and revolution; they do not endorse removal of the king.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Legitimists reject constitutionalism and parliamentary sovereignty; Chambord insisted on the monarchical principle.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Catholic legitimists had no stated doctrine; the Church teaches animals should be treated with kindness but not a moral status of equals; adherents split.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from Catholic and rural-aristocratic tradition, which accepts humane use of animals.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Social Catholic legitimists such as de Mun taught paternal duty of the privileged and class cooperation.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Legitimists were active in counter-revolutionary politics, but aristocratic withdrawal (internal exile) after 1830 was also common; inferred, most favour engagement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed by legitimism, which predates mass media; inferred only loosely from its counter-revolutionary suspicion of modern society.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; legitimists would stress Church and social bodies shaping consent, but did not use the Gramscian frame.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Legitimism has no doctrine on world economy; inferred from its corporatist and anti-socialist stance, which rejects structural-exploitation theories.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from French legitimist nationalism-of-the-kingdom and its Catholic national identity, with the Chambord manifesto emphasising French national unity.

party-own-road.rationale: Legitimists were not communists; the statement is addressed to socialist parties, and legitimists opposed direction from abroad only in the sense of national unity.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the Legitimist emphasis on national sovereignty and local franchises, and suspicion of foreign tutelage.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not part of the legitimist programme after 1830, which focused on the dynastic question; adherents did not stress irredentism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from legitimism's commitment to hereditary aristocratic and Catholic French order, which rejects rule by descent from pre-colonial peoples as foreign to its world.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Legitimists were counter-revolutionary and opposed the republican and revolutionary tradition; they would not make anti-fascism a founding value.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Fascism and communism arose after legitimists' peak; Catholic traditionalists condemn both, but equivalence is not documented in the sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Legitimism took no position on the American Civil War; no stated view.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from legitimism's veneration of tradition, historical continuity and national symbols such as the white flag and fleur-de-lis.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by legitimism; Catholic social teaching stresses family roles and paternal care, with adherents split on this modern framing.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; the Catholic social tradition stresses protection of the family, but no stated position on this framing.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the legitimist rejection of liberalism's universalism and its insistence on France's own historical constitution.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from monarchist traditionalism, which accepts the army as a pillar of throne and order; legitimists mostly opposed military regimes like Bonapartism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Social Catholicism backed family wages and the male-breadwinner household, so legitimists would hesitate to treat domestic work as paid labour; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Catholic paternalist social order stresses family bonds; inferred from the traditionalist outlook.

office-by-exam.rationale: Legitimists defended hereditary rule and aristocratic influence over merit-based selection; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: No Legitimist position on foreign firms; protectionist landed interests and anti-liberal views point different ways.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: As counter-revolutionary Catholics, Legitimists upheld the Church's indissoluble marriage against secular divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: They opposed popular sovereignty and constitutionalism; Chambord stood on the monarchical principle rather than the will of electors.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Social Catholic corporatism favours bodies and class cooperation over individual market accounts; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Legitimists were a landed aristocratic camp that defended inherited estates, not use-based tenure; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Legitimists rejected parliamentary sovereignty but accepted representative bodies under the king; split.

single-official-language.rationale: Chambord's manifesto stresses local franchises and decentralisation, so enforced uniformity of language is disfavoured; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Landed Legitimism favoured keeping the national soil with its own people; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Counter-revolutionary hierarchy rejected egalitarian equality-of-outcome premises; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Social Catholics criticised liberal materialism and acquisitiveness; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Legitimists sympathised with counter-revolutionary causes but had no doctrine on arming rebels; split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The doctrine of legitimacy favoured monarchical solidarity, but no source on forcing allies to stay; split.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from social Catholics such as de Mun, who criticised liberal capitalism and money power; not a documented plank of the wider camp.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from counter-revolutionary suspicion of outside revolutionary influence on the nation; no direct source.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from Catholic family doctrine and social Catholic concern for the family.

residents-only-property.rationale: Legitimists favoured local liberties but defended property rights, so adherents pull both ways; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: The social Catholic strand wanted protective labour measures, but a state job guarantee is not documented; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Counter-revolutionaries rejected republican and democratic principles, so spreading democracy is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from the legitimist emphasis on obedience to rightful, divinely sanctioned authority, as opposed to revolutionary right of resistance.

non-intervention.rationale: Legitimists backed legitimist restoration abroad yet valued sovereignty; no stated position, inferred split.

industrial-unions.rationale: The social Catholic strand favoured corporate bodies uniting employers and workers rather than class unions; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Counter-revolutionary writers blamed Freemasons and others for revolution, but this is not part of the dynastic doctrine; adherents are split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching on marriage as a sacrament, which the Church rather than the state upheld.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the preference for royal authority over liberal transparency; not a stated position.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the agrarian, decentralising and traditional social order the Legitimists defended.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: Legitimists favoured established hierarchical bodies, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; dynastic legitimacy and French sovereignty point in different directions.

religious-nation.rationale: Legitimism is Catholic and tied to the Church's role in the French nation, as in the Chambord manifesto; the national-religion link is inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a monarchist view of France as a sovereign kingdom, though a hierarchy of crowns is not a Legitimist doctrine.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Chambord called for administrative decentralisation and local franchises, which favors regions managing their own resources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Social Catholic Legitimists such as de Mun rejected socialism and defended property and class cooperation.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anachronistic for the 1830-83 scope; inferred from the counter-revolutionary rejection of socialism and Catholic hostility to it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No Legitimist doctrine on service providers; Church charity and state roles pull different ways.

religion-illusion.rationale: Legitimists are counter-revolutionary Catholics who defend the Church and its influence, so they reject the claim that religion is an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from counter-revolutionary distrust of liberal bourgeois society, though de Mun accepted a market economy with reforms.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from Catholic traditionalism and a family-centered social order; the movement did not address women equality.

socialized-care.rationale: De Mun and social Catholics rejected socialism and put the family and Church charity at the center of social care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no settled view on foreign loanwords.

treaties-binding.rationale: Chambord defended local franchises and inherited rights; honoring long-standing agreements is inferred from this legitimist respect for prescriptive right.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Corporate bodies and local liberties are valued, but under a hierarchical monarchy and Church, not common-property communities; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic and decentralist outlook; the sources do not mention settlement policy.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Social Catholic Legitimists sought a path between liberal individualism and socialism through corporate bodies and class cooperation.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the Legitimist claim that dynastic right and historical title outweigh present popular will, applied to a nation's ties to its land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: the movement predates the Holocaust and a Catholic monarchist adherent would reject the claim.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from Catholic moral teaching, with modern adherents divided on criminal law.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: counter-revolutionary and order-minded, yet it itself was the opposition and favoured local liberties.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from the confessional Catholic monarchy the movement wanted, with the Church's influence in public life.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: the movement did not address colonial policy; an adherent could back French overseas rule on royal or Catholic grounds.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: outside the doctrine; Catholic monarchists would not endorse an Islamic armed duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: the Legitimist case against rulers rests on dynastic right, not on religious law, though the movement was counter-revolutionary.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: favoured hierarchy and the crown, with local liberties through decentralisation rather than direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: counter-revolutionary Catholic hierarchy and traditional family roles weigh against this modern analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Catholic moral teaching and traditional social order; anachronistic.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching on the sanctity of life; anachronistic.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: the movement opposed the revolutionary left and the liberal right alike, and a synthesis of the two was not its aim.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: social Catholics from La Tour du Pin and de Mun criticised liberal individualism and the treatment of workers as commodities, though not in Marxist terms.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: Catholic traditionalists regarded Islam as a rival religion; anachronistic for the 19th-century movement.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Chambord's manifesto and Legitimist doctrine hold that kingship is a divine trust passed by hereditary right, not by popular sovereignty.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from Catholic public religion and the Church's place in the state, which opposes banning religious dress.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: social Catholics favoured class cooperation and corporate bodies, with protection of workers within a regulated order.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: a monarchist order rests on royal armies and military strength.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: social Catholics worried about the poor, while the hierarchy accepted rank and wealth; adherents are split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: foreign policy was dynastic and the movement did not address modern blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Legitimism is the claim that the crown passes by hereditary right and the Salic law to the senior Bourbon line, and the Count of Chambord invoked monarchical heredity in his 1871 manifesto.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Legitimists favoured corporate bodies and social Catholic reforms of de Mun, but user-owned cost-price banking is not documented; a mild inference that they would not insist on it.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The statement is anachronistic for 1830-1883; Legitimist emphasis on national independence and Church-led social order does not settle a position on IMF conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Legitimists rejected popular sovereignty and liberal universal suffrage as products of the Revolution; they backed a hierarchical order of estates and notables, though Chambord's manifesto spoke of an elected national voice, so property franchise is an inference.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Legitimist Catholic doctrine upheld the hierarchy of the sexes in the family and treated nature as God's creation, so adherents would reject the claim; this is inferred.

reification.rationale: Legitimism is not Marxist and does not use the concept; social Catholics like de Mun criticised liberal capitalism but also rejected socialism, so no support for the claim.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: De Mun's social Catholics criticised liberal capitalism's effect on workers, but press and assembly rights were not Legitimist concerns, and Legitimists opposed liberal freedoms generally.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Chambord's manifesto favoured a rule bounded by law and local franchises, and the Legitimists opposed arbitrary power while Bourbon rule was monarchical by tradition, but they did not hold to a legal-constitutional view like liberals.

racial-franchise.rationale: Legitimism is dynastic and Catholic, not racial; its claim is to a French royal house over all subjects of the nation, and Chambord's manifesto spoke of national unity.

online-participation.rationale: The statement is anachronistic; Legitimists' preference for hierarchy and rejection of popular sovereignty implies disagreement with direct online decision-making.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; Legitimist monarchists defended the royal prerogative and the secrecy of the state, so open-government data is not part of their doctrine and is inferred as a mild disagreement.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Legitimists upheld the Catholic Church's influence on law and society, and canon law then limited mixed marriages; restriction by law is inferred and not documented in the sources.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Legitimists were Catholic traditionalists, but the sources do not document boycotts of minority shops, and their prime opposition was to liberal revolution; this is a weak inference.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Legitimists rest authority on hereditary right and reject popular sovereignty, as the Chambord manifesto does; choosing decision-makers by lot contradicts their counter-revolutionary order.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Counter-revolutionary Catholic monarchists defend the Church's inherited authority and doctrine against modern liberal rethinking.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Social Catholics from the Legitimist milieu criticised liberal capitalism and urged corporate bodies and duties of employers; inferred, not a stated position on wealth and liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Catholic counter-revolutionary monarchists would likely have kept the traditional bar; the question is anachronistic for 1830-1883.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Legitimists defended the Church and Catholic education against the Revolution's secularism, so state promotion of unbelief is the opposite of their programme.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: As order-and-authority monarchists they backed a strong state with its courts and police; abolition is far outside their thought.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The Chambord manifesto asserts the single hereditary crown and national unity; guaranteed community shares in the executive are inferred to be foreign to this.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Catholic social action favoured Church and voluntary charity and subsidiarity over state provision; inferred from de Mun's social Catholicism.

term-limits.rationale: A hereditary monarchy values permanence and experience over turnover in elected office; inferred, since Legitimists rejected electoral politics as the source of authority.

vote-delegation.rationale: Legitimists rejected popular sovereignty and the Revolution's individualism; inferred that delegable mass voting would be rejected.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses existential risk; no principle clearly pushes either way.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: As Catholic traditionalists they accepted the all-male priesthood and the Church's teaching office as settled.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Catholic traditional family under the husband's headship was assumed by this milieu; inferred, as the sources do not discuss marital authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from Legitimists' rejection of popular-sovereignty and liberal participation doctrines; local franchises were tied to established communities.

rent-control.rationale: No doctrine on this; paternalist social Catholic regulation pulls one way and defence of landed property the other.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the Legitimist defence of property and established rights.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from social Catholics' preference for church-led workers' circles and voluntary associations over state-drilled youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources give nothing to infer from.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anachronistic; Legitimists valued national independence but there is no stated position on basing.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Social Catholics like de Mun defended workers' dignity but also property and class cooperation, so adherents are split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from Catholic teaching, which allows defence of self and others.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from Chambord's appeal to the ancient monarchy as the thread of France's history, against the break of the Revolution.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from traditional Catholic belief in a natural order of the sexes.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from traditional Catholic belief in a natural order of the sexes.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from Catholic veneration of martyrs and the royalist cult of Louis XVI and the royal family as martyrs of the Revolution.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Legitimists framed the Revolution as a Catholic counter-revolutionary struggle against impiety, so this is inferred from that outlook.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; the sources say nothing about a homeland serving a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed; Legitimists sought moral and religious renewal but through restoring the monarchy.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from traditional Catholic usage of Father and King for God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from Catholic reliance on scriptural and Church authority rather than any external test of the scriptures.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Not addressed; Legitimists stressed national unity and class cooperation, not ethnic economic ownership.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from Chambord's call for decentralisation and local franchises and his stress on one France.

independent-unions.rationale: Social Catholic Legitimists favoured workers' circles and corporate bodies mixing classes rather than adversarial unions; inferred, split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Legitimist social Catholics rejected socialism and class struggle; inferred they would not accept worker rule as the test of a just order.

local-essentials-public.rationale: No Legitimist doctrine on utilities; paternal charity and local franchises pull one way, distrust of state expansion the other. Inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from Legitimist rejection of single-assembly liberal parliamentarism and preference for traditional bodies beside the crown.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: Legitimists favoured private property and landed notables, with local franchises in administration, not communal ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Chambord wanted local franchises under a hereditary crown, not towns whose assemblies hold final decisions; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from social Catholicism (de Mun) with its labour reforms and family-centred Catholic social order.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic; no Legitimist position. Inferred as neutral.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anachronistic; no Legitimist position. Inferred as neutral.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Legitimist preference for hierarchy and order over untraceable individual autonomy.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; no Legitimist position. Inferred as neutral.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from Catholic social thought's dignity of the person, though Legitimists also stressed duty to crown, church and corporate bodies.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Legitimists were counter-revolutionary Catholic monarchists who held Church influence and religious order central to politics.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Chambord promised local franchises as guaranteed liberties, while the crown remained sovereign; adherents are split on revocability. Inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; no Legitimist position. Inferred as neutral.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from Legitimism's base among rural landed notables and its suspicion of the revolutionary city.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from Catholic universalism and the national unity of the Chambord manifesto, which stress faith and dynasty over race.

racial-pride.rationale: Anachronistic; Legitimists prized lineage and ancestry in dynastic terms but not racial identity. Inferred as split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from a dynastic, monarchical tradition that did not bind the crown to defence alone.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: Legitimists defined the nation by the dynasty, the Catholic faith and history, with no doctrine of language as the basis of nationhood.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the social Catholic strand of La Tour du Pin and de Mun, which favored representation of corporate bodies and Catholic organizations rather than individuals alone.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the sources give no Legitimist doctrine of foreign partition plots, and Chambord appealed to national unity under the crown.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic wish for Church influence in teaching and the aversion to state expansion in a decentralized monarchy.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine has nothing on environmental taxes and prefers custom and local liberties to new state levies.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the dynastic idea that the crown and its inheritance pass unbroken from generation to generation.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic, hereditary-monarchist outlook, which gave public life to men and did not seek extra weight for women.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: a restored monarchy would keep the army needed for the crown, and the sources show no disarmament doctrine.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the dynastic diplomacy of the old monarchy, which was conducted by the crown in confidence.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: social Catholics favored regulating economic life while Legitimists disliked a centralizing state, so adherents plausibly split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: a restored crown would hold the monopoly of force, so Legitimists would disarm rival armed bodies, though they once raised royalist rebellions themselves.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from counter-revolutionary loyalty to throne, army and order: refusing the sovereign's orders to fight is a revolutionary act.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from de Mun's social Catholic corporatism, which favoured mixed bodies of workers and employers setting conditions collectively over individual contracts.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; paternalist Catholic charity would support helping poor families, while Legitimist fiscal conservatism would resist new transfers, so adherents split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist preference for prudent, orderly royal finances over open-ended borrowing; modern fiscal rules were never discussed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The question of international economic rules was never addressed by Legitimists, and nothing in their principles points either way.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Legitimists are counter-revolutionaries who want the historic monarchy and its institutions restored, not the state apparatus destroyed.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: the Chambord manifesto defends a fixed traditional order, and Catholic social teaching rejects open-ended economic experiments, though local liberties are valued.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a landed, Catholic traditionalist outlook that sees nature as God's creation rather than as capital to be priced.

sacred-nation.rationale: The manifesto presents France as a historic Catholic nation bound to its dynasty across generations, but 'sacred' is stronger than its wording.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Catholic paternalism favouring charity and church schooling over state cancellation of debts.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Legitimists favoured decentralisation and local liberties, but the framing of centre-periphery exploitation as colonialism is foreign to them.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Social Catholicism, which Legitimist de Mun and La Tour du Pin championed, rests on a natural-law view of fixed human nature and dignity.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: Legitimists distrust state-run institutions of opinion and would favour church and private provision over state-funded media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Legitimists were counter-revolutionary Catholics who held the Church to be the one true religion, so a shared-truth view of all religions is foreign to them.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from paternalist social Catholicism (de Mun) and the landed rural base of Legitimism, which favoured protecting farmers over free markets.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a monarchist concern for national strength and independence, which would not accept unilateral disarmament.

workers-own-party.rationale: De Mun's social Catholics sought class cooperation through workers' circles and rejected socialism and class politics, so a separate workers' party runs against that.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Catholic moral order and the protection of persons, though custom-friendly traditionalists might hesitate.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Never addressed; Catholic patriarchal family order pulls against it while Napoleonic equal inheritance was already French law, so adherents are split.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Never addressed; Chambord favoured local franchises but also national unity, and the naming question has no Legitimist position.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Anachronistic; respect for property rights suggests liability for harm while paternalist hierarchy accepts public authority, so no clear lean.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the Legitimist preference for traditional hierarchies and local bodies over mass elected assemblies, as in Chambord's call for decentralisation.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; Legitimists valued the land and stewardship but also distrusted state coercion, so adherents would be split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Never addressed; the order-minded Catholic right favoured firm punishment but the older monarchy relied on judicial discretion.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the Legitimist stress on national unity and French tradition under the monarchy, which would expect settlers to adopt French.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: No Legitimist doctrine on dues; social Catholic workers' circles pull toward corporate bodies, aversion to state compulsion the other way.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; no doctrine on elections beyond rejecting them as the source of authority.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Legitimists were counter-revolutionary Catholics who wanted the Church to hold privileged influence in the state.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Legitimists rejected constitutionalism and popular sovereignty; legitimacy comes from hereditary right, not elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from Catholic moral doctrine, which confined sex to marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis to infer a stable position.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from social Catholic paternalism through charity and corporate bodies rather than state cash systems.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from the Salic law and male-line succession and the traditional order Legitimists defended.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from Catholic counter-revolutionary support for the Church's role in family and society.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not a 19th-century Legitimist issue; no basis to infer a position.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from rejection of state expansion and modern equality doctrines.

homestead-ownership.rationale: No Legitimist doctrine on property acquisition; landed paternalism and respect for established title pull in different directions.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the Legitimist emphasis on royal and national sovereignty and distrust of revolutionary, universalist institutions.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the Legitimists' devout Catholicism; Catholic teaching is not usually literalist, so only mild agreement.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the traditional hierarchical and Catholic social order that Legitimists favor; the sources do not discuss it.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the counter-revolutionary rejection of socialism and the Republic; anachronistic for a 19th-century movement.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from Legitimist rejection of popular sovereignty and the social Catholic preference for corporate bodies over mass voting.

national-church-status.rationale: Legitimists are Catholic monarchists who favor Church influence, so a special status for the national church fits their position.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Legitimists favor administrative decentralisation and local liberties, so regional autonomy fits, though ethnic minorities were not their concern.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of popular sovereignty; Chambord's manifesto rests on hereditary right, not the vote.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Colonial borders are anachronistic for the 1830 to 1883 scope and not addressed in the sources.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; paternalist Catholic ideals of modesty and a hierarchical rural society pull in different directions.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; anachronistic for the scope.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the traditional Catholic social order with distinct roles for men and women; conscription of women is anachronistic.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Counter-revolutionary Legitimists valued land, soil and tradition (Chambord's attachment to local franchises); inferred, not a stated doctrine.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Catholic, order-minded Legitimists favoured legal monarchy and traditional justice; inferred opposition to killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: A 19th-century French royalist question about China is anachronistic; inferred preference for traditional European alliances.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Legitimists had no stated policy on kin minorities abroad; anachronistic and neutral.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Legitimists defended hereditary property and rejected revolutionary levelling; inferred that equal common ownership is opposed.

self-ownership.rationale: Legitimists rejected liberal individualism in favour of corporate bodies, Church and family; inferred rejection of full self-ownership.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: No stated Legitimist position on consumption taxes; anachronistic.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Albert de Mun's social Catholicism favoured paternalist protection of workers and the poor; inferred support for aid aimed at the poor.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Chambord and de Mun valued intermediate bodies, local franchises and workers' circles between king and people, so bypassing them is rejected.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Legitimists opposed the Orleanist bourgeois regime and its financial interests; inferred opposition to privileged business ties.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Legitimists wanted Catholic Church influence on the state, so politics is not kept free of confessional lines.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Legitimist social Catholics accepted industrial society while upholding tradition and religion; inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Legitimists were Catholic counter-revolutionaries who rejected the secular revolutionary legacy, including civil divorce, in line with Catholic doctrine on marriage.

national-resource-control.rationale: No stated Legitimist position on resources; anachronistic.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from the Legitimist respect for inherited right and property; the sources do not discuss distributive justice.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: No Legitimist doctrine on international finance; paternalist social Catholicism and distrust of speculation are balanced by aversion to state expansion.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: An anachronistic question the sources never address; nothing in Legitimist doctrine settles it.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from Catholic natural-law thinking and the Legitimist view that the post-1830 regimes lacked rightful authority.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic; social Catholics cared for workers' welfare but nothing is said on automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: The sources do not address world order; counter-revolutionary monarchism neither endorses nor opposes a balance of powers.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: No Legitimist doctrine on value theory; social Catholics stressed the dignity of labour but did not adopt such a theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Chambord's manifesto stressed national unity and de Mun's workers' circles joined Catholic patriotism with working-class welfare; inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: A debate within the modern left; Legitimists have no stance on it.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from Legitimist rejection of single-party and revolutionary rule and of socialism.

missingStatements.text: The rightful ruler is determined by hereditary succession in a royal line, not by election or popular consent.
missingStatements.rationale: Succession by Salic law and primogeniture to the senior Capetian line is the defining Legitimist claim, and Chambord invoked the national principle of monarchical heredity.

missingStatements.text: A deposed dynasty keeps its right to the throne even after a revolution and a long period of other rule.
missingStatements.rationale: Legitimists treat the 1830 revolution as void against the senior Bourbon line and hold that the crown passes at once on a monarch's death and cannot be renounced.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the French legitimist dynastic claim; too niche to ask of every ideology.

missingStatements.text: A national flag may be an inseparable symbol of the legitimacy of the regime and should not be compromised for political convenience.
missingStatements.rationale: Chambord refused the crown rather than accept the tricolour, declaring that Henri V cannot abandon the white flag of Henri IV.
missingStatements.declined: About a single national flag in one historical episode; too niche to ask of every ideology.

notes: Fusionist Legitimists accepted the Orleanist heir, and the later Ralliement (de Mun, 1892) accepted the Republic. The profile represents the unreconciled strand, with modern Catholic traditionalist adherents inferred.
